Operate

Development

Lint, types, frontend checks, and the coverage map.

Everything below mirrors what CI runs. Install the workspace first:

uv sync --all-packages

Linting, Formatting & Type Checks#

Shared tooling lives in the root pyproject.toml, so one command covers every Python project:

uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy apps packages
uv run --directory website mypy .

# Security scanning
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages website/

Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio)#

The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally:

npm --prefix apps/studio run lint        # ESLint
npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run   # Vitest on jsdom (run once)
npm --prefix apps/studio run test:visual # Vitest Browser Mode → Chromatic archives
npm --prefix apps/studio run build       # production build → apps/studio/dist
cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check

Visual tests#

npm test runs the jsdom suite and deliberately ignores *.visual.test.tsx. Those files render one component state in Chromium under vitest.visual.config.ts, and the Chromatic workflow publishes them on every branch push so a reviewer can compare pixels component by component. Each test costs one billed snapshot per build on the free 5,000/month allowance, which is why the two suites are split by filename instead of running every test in a browser. Browser mode needs Chromium locally: npx playwright install chromium. See Deployment for the project setup and budget rules.

Website Checks (GitHub Pages)#

The website/ static site is part of the main CI workflow. Its tests assert the committed OG art is reproducible and that the publish pipeline (website/tests/test_pages_deploy.py) still exists:

uv run --directory website pytest tests/

The site is generated at CI time and never committed. CI runs build_site.py to produce _site and uploads it as the website-site artifact for review.

Publishing happens in .github/workflows/pages.yml: it runs those tests, builds _site from website/, and deploys the artifact with actions/deploy-pages on every push to main. There is no gh-pages branch, so that workflow is the only thing that keeps https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/ online.

Formatting workflow#

  • When editing Python files, either rely on the pre-commit hooks below (recommended) or run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:

    uv run ruff format .

  • CI behavior:

    • CI runs uv run ruff check . to lint without modifying files.
    • CI runs uv run ruff format --check . to verify formatting only.
    • If CI fails on formatting, run uv run ruff format . locally, commit the changes, and push again.

Pre-commit hooks#

To run the checks automatically before each commit:

uv tool install pre-commit
pre-commit install

After this, ruff and ruff-format run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually:

pre-commit run --all-files

Testing#

Tests use pytest with pytest-asyncio (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Tests live next to the package they cover, and every test runs from the repository root:

uv run pytest                        # everything
uv run pytest apps/cli               # one app
uv run pytest packages/core          # one package
uv run pytest tests/contract         # cross-package contracts
uv run pytest tests/scripts          # dev launcher

The MCP server contract test compares the live FastMCP registry with packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py, so add or change a tool in both places. The CLI local-backend contract test keeps _LOCAL_HANDLERS aligned with the same tool names.

Test Coverage#

CI runs the suite on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 and uploads one combined coverage.xml from the 3.12 job to Codecov.

The Codecov upload authenticates with the CODECOV_TOKEN repository secret and is non-blocking (fail_ci_if_error: false), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README tracks main, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:

  • Project status requires at least 90% coverage (target: 90%) and tolerates a 1% dip from codecov.yml.
  • Patch status is informational for now, so new code can land while the suite catches up.

To reproduce the report locally:

uv run pytest \
  --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
  --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
  --cov=agentic_odi_core \
  --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
  --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
  --cov-report=term-missing \
  --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

[!NOTE] Coverage is only collected for the Python packages. apps/studio/ and test directories are excluded in codecov.yml.

Conventions#

  • Test files live under each project's tests/ directory and are named test_*.py.
  • Root tests/ is reserved for cross-package checks (contract/ and scripts/).
  • Every async test is decorated with @pytest.mark.asyncio.
  • Use Client(mcp) directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
  • The MCP server's reset_db autouse fixture clears in-memory state before each test.

Test Coverage Map#

Area What it covers
packages/core/tests/ Domain models, opportunity scoring, ODIService, repository implementations, SQLite persistence, schema, and repository factory
apps/mcp-server/tests/ Full ODI workflow, entity parity, context tools, Customer Outcomes, evidence, tool errors, and HTTP transport startup
apps/studio-api/tests/ Health, config, canvas, SSE chat, SPA fallback, MCP hydration, probes, and step/outcome passthrough
apps/cli/tests/ Backend selection, local/remote CRUD, chat, wizard, onboarding, updates, rendering, connectors, and startup performance
packages/connectors/tests/ Catalog presets, registry persistence, factory, MCP and REST connectors, evidence mapping, and sink
tests/contract/ Live MCP tool surface and CLI local-handler parity
tests/scripts/ scripts/dev.py startup, port checks, signals, and shutdown
apps/studio/src/**/*.test.ts SPA units: ODI math, transport bridge, SSE parser, sidecar client
apps/studio/src/**/*.visual.test.tsx Component states captured for Chromatic visual review
website/tests/ Static site integrity, OG art reproducibility, and README sync

[!TIP] Type /test in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically.

Agent Session Tracking#

Agent sessions are captured with the Entire CLI. The repository integration lives in .entire/settings.json, .cursor/hooks.json, and .opencode/plugins/entire.ts. Run entire status to confirm it is enabled and entire checkpoint list to inspect captured checkpoints.
